book.title: The Telegraph All New Toughie Crossword, book 1

clue.text: Train I halt on the hour, taking the high ground?

indicators.note: to train something is to shape or drill it into a new form, so the words that follow are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written, letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A railway passenger complains that the train stops every hour on its climb into the hills.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Train' looks like the railway vehicle, but it is the instruction to rearrange I HALT ON THE HOUR into HOLIER-THAN-THOU.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone smugly claiming moral superiority is said to take the moral high ground, the attitude of a sanctimonious person.

clue.text: Morally pure but heartless family group

indicators.note: without a heart means the central letter of the word is taken out

blocks.note: clean can mean free of sin or immorality

explanation.surface: A household that is virtuous yet cold and uncaring.
explanation.walkthrough: CLEAN loses its middle letter E to give CLAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A clan is a group of related households, especially in Scotland, claiming descent from one ancestor.

clue.text: Many quotations are attributed so shortly

blocks.note: first meaning: the abbreviation for anonymous, credited when the author is unknown
second meaning: an old word for soon, in a little while

explanation.surface: A remark that lots of quotations are credited briefly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shortly' seems to say the attribution is brief, as an abbreviation is, but it is a separate meaning: soon.
explanation.definitionFit: The abbreviated form of anonymous stands under unattributed sayings, and the archaic adverb means soon or presently.

clue.text: Loads of money promoting song

blocks.note: to be for something is to support or promote it
a tune is a melody or song

explanation.surface: A huge sum of cash spent on pushing a hit record.
explanation.definitionFit: A fortune is a very large amount of wealth, as in 'it cost a fortune'.

clue.text: Dominant nation which defines a comic-book hero?

blocks.note: first meaning: a country with overwhelming global influence
second meaning, playful: the special ability that marks out a caped crusader

explanation.surface: A leading country whose identity is like that of a cartoon champion.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the second sense: comic-book heroes are defined by their extraordinary abilities.
explanation.definitionFit: A superpower is both a state such as the USA with worldwide dominance and a superhuman ability like flight.

clue.text: Inhospitable region's line in unusual wines (reds)

indicators.note: something unusual is out of its normal form, so the letters are rearranged
one element sits inside the other, enclosed by its letters

blocks.note: taken as written, part of the letters to rearrange
taken as written, the rest of the letters to rearrange
L is the standard abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: A wine list for some bleak area features odd red varieties.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracket around 'reds' is only surface dressing: the word is plain fodder, not a hint about colour.
explanation.definitionFit: A wilderness is wild uncultivated land, hostile to settlement.

clue.text: Italian romance fools around or somehow pulls one in

indicators.note: somehow means in some unspecified way, so the preceding words are rearranged
pulls in means draws something inside, so a piece is taken into the rest

blocks.note: taken as written, letters to be rearranged
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An Italian love affair in which a playboy flirts or somehow lures someone in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Around' looks like the anagram signal, but it is part of the fodder; the word after 'or' does the rearranging.
explanation.definitionFit: Ariosto's epic poem of 1532 is a chivalric romance about the paladin Roland driven mad by love.

clue.text: Moving top of leg, arm etc, it's used

definitions.text: Moving top of leg, arm etc, it's used

indicators.note: moving means shifting position, so the letters change places
the top of a word in a down clue is its first letter

blocks.note: the first letter of leg
taken as written, letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A description of what is used to move the upper leg, arms and other limbs.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: the voluntary muscles that move the limbs.
explanation.definitionFit: Striated or skeletal muscle, banded under the microscope, is the tissue that contracts to move legs and arms.

clue.text: Flowery growth of grand music for large group, in small part

indicators.note: one part is placed inside another, surrounded by its letters

blocks.note: a mite is a tiny piece or amount
G is slang for a grand, a thousand pounds or dollars
a nonet is a piece for nine players

explanation.surface: A grand floral display of music for a big ensemble, in a minor role.
explanation.walkthrough: A nonet is music for nine players, which counts as a large group for chamber music; G for grand is slang for a thousand.
explanation.definitionFit: Mignonette is a garden plant grown for its fragrant spikes of small flowers.

clue.text: Strange description of …

blocks.note: first meaning: peculiar, weird
second meaning: the ellipsis carries on into the next clue, 14 Down, a number this word describes

explanation.walkthrough: The dots link to 14 Down, NUMBER NINE: nine is an odd number, so the word describes it.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means peculiar, and also names whole numbers not divisible by two, such as nine.

clue.text: Brunette departs with rescue ship

blocks.note: D is the timetable abbreviation for departs
Noah's ark saved its passengers from the Flood

explanation.surface: A brown-haired woman sets off on a lifeboat.
explanation.definitionFit: A brunette has dark hair, so the adjective describes her colouring.

clue.text: Pity 16 in Verdun

blocks.note: first meaning: regret or sorrow, as a noun
second meaning: the French word for the answer to 16 Across, Verdun being a French town

explanation.surface: Sorrow at the street fighting in a French battlefield town.
explanation.walkthrough: 16 Across is ROAD, and Verdun signals French: the French for street.
explanation.definitionFit: Rue is an old noun for sorrow or compassion, and it is also the French word for a street.

clue.text: Biscuit variety with flower on its back?

indicators.note: lying on its back turns a word over, so in an across clue it is read from right to left

blocks.note: a brand is a make or kind of product
the pansy is a garden flower

explanation.surface: A type of cookie decorated with a flower lying upside down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Biscuit variety' reads as one phrase, but the definition is 'Biscuit' alone and 'variety' starts the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A brandy snap is a crisp rolled ginger biscuit, often filled with cream.

clue.text: … house next to prime minister's that cleared soldiers out?

blocks.note: first meaning: the Downing Street house beside the prime minister's Number Ten
second meaning, playful: the British Army's notorious laxative pill

explanation.surface: The building beside Downing Street that was emptied of troops.
explanation.walkthrough: The British Army's 'Number Nine' pill was a laxative handed out for almost any complaint, so it 'cleared soldiers out'; the dots carry on from 10 Down, ODD.
explanation.definitionFit: 9 Downing Street sits beside Number 10, the prime minister's residence in London, and the army laxative shared the name.

clue.text: Let opponent score when stress can no longer be supported

definitions.text: when stress can no longer be supported

blocks.note: first meaning: to concede or give up a point in a game

blocks.clueFragment: when stress can no longer be supported
blocks.note: second meaning: the engineering term for the load at which a material starts to deform permanently

explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is the phrase read as a verb and its object; the second is a noun from materials science.
explanation.definitionFit: In physics a material's yield point is the stress beyond which it stops springing back and deforms permanently.

clue.text: Pole spanning a thoroughfare

indicators.note: something spanning another stretches right across it, enclosing it

blocks.note: a rod is a pole, also an old unit of length
taken as written

explanation.surface: A beam stretched across a street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' tempts one towards N or S or a Polish person; here it is a rod.
explanation.definitionFit: A road is a public way for travel, which is what thoroughfare means.

clue.text: Sound of a bell ringing new year: it's often on a rooftop

indicators.note: ringing here means forming a ring around, so one piece encircles another

blocks.note: a chime is the ringing note of a bell
N is the abbreviation for new
Y is the abbreviation for year

explanation.surface: Church bells pealing in the New Year, heard from a roof.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ringing' looks like the bell's own sound, but it means encircling: CHIME goes round N, then Y follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A chimney stack, carrying smoke from a fireplace, typically rises from a house roof.

clue.text: Defender's small cry, a hesitant sound

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
to weep is to cry
er is the noise of someone hesitating

explanation.surface: A footballer lets out a quiet, faltering whimper.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's means 'is': the defender is the sum of the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: In football a sweeper is a free defensive player stationed behind the back line.

clue.text: Discovered in hotel, lingerie is significant

indicators.note: discovered in means found inside the words that follow, spanning a gap

blocks.note: the run of letters across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: Finding underwear in a hotel room is revealing.
explanation.definitionFit: A telling detail is one that is revealing or striking, so it has real significance.

clue.text: Joint originally named after king

blocks.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
née marks a woman's birth name, as in 'Mrs Smith, née Jones'

explanation.surface: A cannabis cigarette first called after a monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Originally' does not pick out a first letter here: 'originally named' together is née.
explanation.definitionFit: The knee is the joint between thigh and lower leg.

clue.text: Dull, archaic breed lives in top of St Paul's

definitions.note: 'archaic' marks the answer as an old-fashioned word for dull

indicators.note: one group of letters is placed inside another

blocks.note: the great dome crowns St Paul's Cathedral in London
to rear animals is to breed them
is means exists or lives

explanation.surface: A monotonous old-fashioned way of raising life atop the cathedral.
explanation.walkthrough: St Paul's Cathedral in London is famous for its great dome; 'archaic' belongs with the definition, flagging an old-fashioned word.
explanation.definitionFit: Drearisome is an old variant of dreary, meaning gloomy and tedious.

clue.text: That is embodying cold

indicators.note: to embody something is to contain it within one's body

blocks.note: i.e. abbreviates id est, Latin for that is
C is the tap abbreviation for cold

explanation.surface: Something that personifies chilliness.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: frozen water is the very embodiment of cold.
explanation.definitionFit: Ice is frozen water, a by-word for coldness, so it embodies chill.

clue.text: Declamatory music criticism

blocks.note: first meaning: the hip-hop style of rhythmic spoken lyrics
second meaning: a rebuke

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a critic reviewing showy music; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Rap is rhymed speech over a beat, and a rap is also a sharp reproof.

clue.text: Large country without a prominent feature

indicators.note: without means lacking, so a letter is left out

blocks.note: a vast nation in east Asia
taken as written, the letter to be removed

explanation.surface: A big nation lacking any landmark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Large' looks like L, but 'Large country' together is CHINA, which loses its A.
explanation.definitionFit: The chin is a part of the face that juts out, a prominent facial feature.

clue.text: Poles are flat out in this work, missing start and being behind schedule

definitions.text: Poles are flat out in this

indicators.note: missing its start means the first letter of the word is dropped

blocks.note: a job is a piece of work
the state of running late

explanation.surface: Polish workers sprawled exhausted on the job, falling behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poles' are the ends of a sphere's axis, not people from Poland; a sphere flattened at the poles is oblate.
explanation.definitionFit: Oblateness is the property of a spheroid like the Earth that is squashed at its poles.

clue.text: Test temperature in the form of Kelvin

blocks.note: T is the abbreviation for temperature
as means in the role or form of
K is the symbol for the kelvin unit

explanation.surface: A physics exam on temperature measured in kelvins.
explanation.definitionFit: A task is a piece of set work, and to task someone is to test or strain them.

clue.text: Imperative for audience attacked with 20

indicators.note: something intended for an audience is heard rather than read

blocks.note: 20 Across is a leg joint, so attacked with it means struck with that joint

explanation.surface: A command shouted to spectators as a player is hit by a knee.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference points to 20 Across, KNEE; being kneed sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A need is a necessity or requirement, which is what an imperative is as a noun.

clue.text: To stimulate a single woman, the Spanish spin around

blocks.note: to turn on is to excite or arouse
one is a single unit
she is the pronoun for a woman
el is the Spanish for the

explanation.surface: A man trying to arouse a Spanish single lady who whirls away.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay divides at different points from the answer's own word breaks, so 'a single woman' is not one piece.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn on one's heel is to pivot abruptly and walk away, a sudden spin round.
